children.label: Neuromuscular junction
children: Motor nerve ending, synaptic cleft (20-30 nm), folded muscle membrane, nicotinic receptors
Action potential, Ca2+ influx, ACh exocytosis, ACh binds receptor
Cation influx depolarizes the fiber, Na+ channels fire an action potential
Acetylcholinesterase breaks ACh into acetate and choline

children.label: Classification
children: Spasmolytics relieve spasm toward normal tone
Neuromuscular blockers paralyze muscle completely
Depolarizing: succinylcholine, agonist
Non-depolarizing: competitive antagonists (e.g. tubocurarine)
Ultra-short: succinylcholine; short: mivacurium
Intermediate: vecuronium, rocuronium, atracurium, cisatracurium; long: pancuronium

children.label: Role in surgery
children: Given with anesthetics at induction
Facilitate intra-abdominal and intrathoracic surgery and intubation
All respiratory muscles are paralyzed: ventilation must be available

children.label: Succinylcholine
children: Binds nicotinic receptors: depolarization, fasciculations, then desensitization and paralysis
Broken down by plasma pseudocholinesterase, not acetylcholinesterase
Intubating dose 1-2 mg/kg IV, peak within 60 s, lasts 5-10 min
No antagonist; prolonged in cholinesterase deficiency, liver disease, pregnancy
Indications: full stomach or emergency, cesarean, predicted difficult intubation, ECT, short procedures

children.label: Succinylcholine adverse effects
children: Raised intraocular and intracranial pressure
Myalgia, myoglobinuria, masseter spasm
Bradycardia, dysrhythmia, sinus arrest
Hyperkalemia: normal rise 0.5 mEq/L, up to 13 in high-risk patients
High risk: extensive burns, severe closed head injury, UMN lesion, muscular dystrophy, traumatic paralysis
Contraindications: cannot maintain airway, allergy, MH history, K+ 5.5 or more, myotonia

children.label: Non-depolarizing blockers
children: Compete with ACh at the same receptor; onset 3-4 min
Paralysis order: face and eyes, fingers and limbs, neck and trunk, intercostals, diaphragm last
Recovery in reverse order; given IV only
Prolonged by acidosis, hypothermia, age, low K+ or Ca2+, volatile agents
Reversed with neostigmine plus atropine

children.label: Individual drugs
children: Vecuronium: intermediate, no CVS effects
Rocuronium: onset under 1 min at 0.6 mg/kg, choice when succinylcholine is contraindicated
Cisatracurium: Hofmann degradation, no histamine release, ideal in renal or hepatic failure
Atracurium: releases histamine (avoid in asthmatics)
Pancuronium: long-acting, raises HR and BP, renal excretion

children.label: Anticholinergics
children: Atropine: muscarinic antagonist, crosses BBB, minimum 20 mcg/kg (less causes paradoxical bradycardia)
Atropine effects: tachycardia, mydriasis, dry mouth, bronchodilation, hyperthermia
Overdose: hot as a hare, mad as a hatter, red as a beet, dry as a bone
Atropine uses: block neostigmine effects, reduce secretions, organophosphate antidote
Avoid in closed-angle glaucoma and prostatic hyperplasia
Scopolamine: more CNS effect, amnesia, motion sickness
Glycopyrrolate: most commonly used, no CNS effect, less CV stimulation

children.label: Cholinesterase inhibitors
children: Prolong ACh life; reversible (neostigmine, physostigmine), irreversible (echothiophate)
Neostigmine: most commonly used, 2.5-5 mg IV to reverse non-depolarizing block
Side effects: bradycardia, miosis, salivation, bronchospasm, GI hypermotility
Give atropine with neostigmine in one syringe
Other uses: urinary retention after GA, myasthenia gravis
